name: needs-morale-visual
description: Visual check of morale effects from need gauges: after 200+ ticks without rest, morale should decrease as gauges drain below thresholds; needs command and scores output verify need penalty calculation and well-rested bonus when all gauges above 80

steps.description: #1379: the default site policy (shift_8h, fatigue threshold 60) is always in force, so a staffed crew is force-rested on the shift clock or once fatigue reaches 60. This file is not about shift or rest policy, so continuous mode with the lowest threshold neutralizes it and the file keeps testing what it was written for.

expect.note: well-rested bonus: at 100 ticks all gauges are still above 80, morale rises to 100 and wellBeing jumps toward its cap — confirms the file's own claimed bonus, not just the eventual penalty

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

expect.note: gauges have now drained below thresholds — morale and wellBeing both fall from their tick-100 peak, confirming the penalty side of the file's claim #1907: wellBeing is no longer asserted here -- union events run on their own cooldown clock, Food Trucks now halts this batch at tick 120 and wellBeing is still pinned at its ~100 cap; the penalty is asserted below, where the gauges actually drain it.

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

expect.note: #2146: minor events are non-blocking notices now, so ticks no longer halt at them and the old 200-tick batch ran the crew through a mid-batch rest (minFatigue rose) and into the worker revolt that ends the level (tick 376). Batch shortened to 20 ticks, ahead of the rest; the continuing drain shows as wellBeing falling from 45.5 toward 0.

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.
#1996: drain phase. #2146: minor events are non-blocking notices and no longer halt the batch; it is shortened to 30 ticks so the final 100-tick step still ends ahead of the tick-376 worker revolt.
Resolve a pending major event if any (minor events are notices since #2146 and never block ticks).

expect.note: gauges have drained below thresholds -- #2146: wellBeing already hit 0 in the tick-20 step above (falls from its ~100 cap to 0 by ~tick 230) and the decrease is asserted there; here it stays pinned at 0 (minFatigue is not asserted: the crew rests mid-batch), confirming the penalty side of the file's claim. #1996: stopped at 100 ticks rather than 300 -- with union events gated on player actions and their cooldown none lands before the worker revolt (wellBeing 0 for 120 ticks, tick 382) ends the level, so the batch must end ahead of it.

steps.description: #1996: resolve whatever event is pending, if any. The old claim (union_suggestion_box lifting wellBeing from 0) no longer has an event to land on -- the union cooldown outlasts the drain's revolt clock -- so this step only clears a pending dialog and asserts nothing about wellBeing.
